The rust flagship: ban std::mem::forget on a Drop value (clippy restriction-lint mem_forget), distinct from #977's std::env::var firing convention. Rendered by the ADOPTED cargo clippy.toml backend (renderCargoClippy, #977-owned) into a disallowed-methods entry — kind:'method', path:'std::mem::forget', defaultSeverity:'warning' (the only severity render-clippy renders rather than degrades). Session-side render + local `cargo clippy` RED live-fire = LG-S3 Inc 2. LIVE-RESEARCHED, not asserted from memory (§Qc, T3/T12).

rust.official.excerpt: Takes ownership and "forgets" about the value without running its destructor. Any resources the value manages, such as heap memory or a file handle, will linger forever in an unreachable state. `forget` is not marked as `unsafe`, because Rust's safety guarantees do not include a guarantee that destructors will always run.

clippy.excerpt: clippy restriction-group lint `mem_forget`: checks for usage of std::mem::forget(t) where t implements Drop; discouraged because forgetting a Drop value skips its destructor, leaking the resources it manages (confirmed via rust-lang.github.io; the lint index is a JS-rendered SPA so the machine-readable body is captured here from the confirmed lint semantics rather than a raw-markdown scrape).

title: Do not use std::mem::forget() on a Drop value; it skips the destructor and leaks the resource — drop explicitly or use ManuallyDrop
